summary: Iteration 8 — Snapchat OAuth (production Client ID 383e7c1e-...) + Expo Push register/unregister + admin broadcast push integration. Backend: 17/17 pytest green (test_iteration8_snap_push.py). GET /api/auth/snapchat/start returns a valid https://accounts.snapchat.com/accounts/oauth2/auth URL with client_id=383e7c1e-..., redirect_uri ending in /auth/snapchat/callback, response_type=code, state, code_challenge (S256, base64url ~43 chars), code_challenge_method=S256, and the required Snap scopes (user.display_name, user.bitmoji.avatar, user.external_id). POST /api/auth/snapchat/callback rejects unknown state with 400 and missing fields with 422 (real OAuth round-trip not automatable). POST /api/push/register requires auth (401 without bearer), validates expo_token min_length=10 (422), upserts by expo_token (idempotent, returns success:true). DELETE /api/push/unregister requires auth and removes the row (success:true). POST /api/admin/notifications/broadcast now also fires expo_send_push asynchronously and the response includes push_devices count (verified >=1 after registering a token). Auth required for broadcast (non-admin gets 403). Regression: register, login, admin login, forgot-password, X OAuth start (twitter.com/i/oauth2/authorize), X callback unknown-state 400, /api/meta/categories, /api/meta/countries — all green. Frontend smoke: /login renders Google + X + Snapchat buttons with data-testids. Snapchat button is now real (yellow Snap-styled), 'قيد المراجعة' badge fully removed (count=0). startSnap() wired to GET /auth/snapchat/start and redirects via window.location.href = auth_url.

critical_code_review_comments: Good: /auth/snapchat/start uses secrets.token_urlsafe(16) for state and 96-char code_verifier with SHA-256 challenge — matches RFC 7636 PKCE.
Good: snap_oauth_states record carries expires_at (10 min TTL); callback rotates state via delete_one before token exchange (prevents replay).
Good: callback exchanges code at https://accounts.snapchat.com/login/oauth2/access_token with HTTP Basic auth header (client_id:client_secret) AND code_verifier — correct.
Good: Snap user-info via POST https://kit.snapchat.com/v1/me with GraphQL { me { externalId displayName bitmoji { avatar } } } — uses externalId as the stable Snap user key.
Good: Placeholder email pattern snap_{external_id}@snapchat.local mirrors X's x_{x_id}@x.local — consistent strategy. Same caveat: blocks future email comms until user updates email.
Good: user.pop('_id', None) before returning from snap callback — no Mongo ObjectId leak.

Good: /push/register uses upsert by expo_token — idempotent, won't duplicate per-device records on re-login. Updates user_id on each upsert, so token rotation between users on the same device is handled correctly.
Good: expo_send_push is fire-and-forget via asyncio.create_task in broadcast — won't block the admin's HTTP response if Expo is slow.

Minor: expo_send_push catches all Exceptions and only logs — doesn't surface a partial failure to the admin endpoint. push_devices in the broadcast response is the COUNT of registered devices, not the number Expo accepted. Acceptable for v1, but consider returning an Expo ticket-id list for receipt polling later.
Minor: /push/register has no per-user limit. A malicious authenticated client could insert thousands of bogus expo_token rows. Consider a hard cap per user_id (e.g., 10 most-recent device tokens).

Minor: Snap OAuth scope URLs are URL-encoded with a manual replace chain (' ' → '+', ':' → '%3A', '/' → '%2F'). Works for the current scope literals but is fragile — prefer urllib.parse.urlencode or quote_plus.

Minor: redirect_uri derives from FRONTEND_URL env or request.base_url; the .env now has FRONTEND_URL=https://platform-inspect.preview.emergentagent.com (good). Production deploy must override FRONTEND_URL=https://alhraj.online before going live.
No SNAPCHAT_CONFIDENTIAL_CLIENT_ID is currently used in code (only SNAPCHAT_CLIENT_ID + SNAPCHAT_CLIENT_SECRET). The duplicate env var is harmless but dead — remove or document its purpose.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Snapchat OAuth backend is fully wired with the real production Client ID. End-to-end browser flow cannot be automated (Snap login page requires real consent). To verify manually: click Snapchat button on /login → browser navigates to accounts.snapchat.com/accounts/oauth2/auth?client_id=383e7c1e-...&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fplatform-inspect.preview.emergentagent.com%2Fauth%2Fsnapchat%2Fcallback&... → after user authorizes (assuming the callback URI is whitelisted in Snap Dev Portal), browser returns to /auth/snapchat/callback?code=...&state=... → SnapAuthCallback.js POSTs to /api/auth/snapchat/callback → session cookies set + user redirected. Push notifications: backend /push/register + /push/unregister are confirmed. The /app/mobile/src/notifications.js Expo wiring is for the mobile app and was explicitly out-of-scope for this iteration. The next iteration could add an Expo push 'receipt' polling job and per-user device cap. Pytest file /app/backend/tests/test_iteration8_snap_push.py contains the full regression suite — keep it.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no new bugs. One initial test failure (test_push_unregister_requires_auth returned 200 instead of 401) was a TEST artifact: the session-scoped requests.Session was reused across the admin-token fixture, so the unauth test inadvertently carried admin auth cookies. Fixed by using a fresh requests.delete() with no shared cookies. Backend dependency get_current_user is correct.
